# Numeric determinism allowlist: the reviewed exceptions to the
# repo-wide scans in internal/testutil/fmagate (TestFMAReport_RepoWide,
# heavy tier, and TestBannedMathReport_RepoWide, fast tier).
#
# One entry per line:
#
#   <kind> <file> <func> <reason...>
#
#   kind    "fma"          a multiply-add the arm64 compiler contracts
#                          (the -d=fmahash=vy report);
#           "math.<Name>"  a reference to a banned stdlib transcendental
#                          (fmagate.BannedMath: Exp, Log, Log1p, Expm1,
#                          Pow, Erf, Erfc, Lgamma, Sin, Cos, Tan, Atan,
#                          ...; math.Sqrt and the other IEEE-exact
#                          functions are never findings).
#   file    module-relative, forward slashes, e.g.
#           internal/processing/test_stat.go
#   func    the enclosing TOP-LEVEL declaration: "F" for a function,
#           "T.M" for a method (pointer and type parameters dropped),
#           "(package)" for a package-level initialiser. A closure counts
#           as the function that holds it.
#   reason  required; why the site cannot or need not be deterministic
#           (control-only, fixture generator, gonum residual, ...).
#
# An entry excuses EVERY finding of its kind in that function of that
# file, so it survives line drift. An entry whose file is in the scanned
# scope but excuses no finding is STALE and fails the scan: delete it
# when the site is fixed. A malformed or duplicate line fails too.
#
# Report one package or file set (each story's "clean in the report"):
#
#   go test -tags heavy -count=1 -v ./internal/testutil/fmagate \
#     -run 'TestFMAReport_RepoWide|TestBannedMathReport_RepoWide' \
#     -fmareport.pkg=./internal/processing/...
#
# -fmareport.pkg takes comma-separated patterns: ./... (default),
# ./a/b/... , ./a/b , or ./a/b/c.go files.
#
# Both scans are BINDING: an unlisted finding fails, naming the site,
# its function and the fix (detmath twin, float64(...) barrier, or an
# entry here).

math.Exp internal/examples/fixtures/gen.go writeExperiment offline generator (//go:build ignore, run by hand with go run, compiled into no Pulse package or test binary) of the checked-in example CSVs; every figure reads the committed CSV bytes, never this code, so no result depends on the arch it runs on (a regeneration may move a last ulp: regenerate on one arch and commit the CSVs)

fma internal/testutil/invariance/invariance.go Within tolerance comparator of a test helper imported only by _test files: it fuses rel*max into the bound of |a-b| <= abs + rel*max(|a|,|b|), which is never a result figure; a last-ulp move of the bound can flip a verdict only for a difference exactly at the documented tolerance
